new:
An applicability failure ends the run with status FAILED and internal stop reason `EDIT_NOT_APPLICABLE`. At main `31c6de5` (#576) the ACP prompt response for that turn has wire `stopReason` `end_turn`, not `refusal`, and `_meta` `{"runStopReason": "EDIT_NOT_APPLICABLE", "outcome": "failed"}` (#559 / PR #569; #268 / PR #561; `acp/spec.py:4135`, `:4278–4308`). This holds for a binding failure before approval and for an applicability failure after it. If a cancel was accepted first, `_meta.outcome` is `cancelled` instead, and before approval `stopReason` is `cancelled` too (`acp/spec.py:2514–2526`; `acp/lifecycle.py:337–341`). The stopped run's text is never sent as a plan: a binding failure sends no plan update, and after approval no completed-plan update is sent, because only a COMPLETED run sends one (#570 / PR #630; `acp/spec.py:3967–3969`, `:4019–4028`).

The completion text is one fixed message per code, built only from the code and the path the plan named, never file content (#574; `agent/edits.py:28–52`, `:66–76`). It is a single line, wrapped here:

```text
The change was not made to <path>, because <reason>.
The plan made no changes and ran none of its tests. <next step>. (<code>)
```

Each code has its own `<reason>` and `<next step>`. For example, `EDIT_OLD_NOT_FOUND` gives "the lines it replaces are not in the file exactly as planned" and "Send your request again to get a new plan".

old: Completion text is passed through by `acp/spec.py:2121–2122`.
